title: A Light for Wrackholm
description: Wrackholm's beacon, the Wrack Light, has been dark since the Snuffing, and nobody on the island has answered a horn since.

stages.text: Nobody on Wrackholm has answered a horn since the Snuffing. The yard is dark, the Wrack Light out on the Teeth is dark, and the answering horn by the lane-house door, which Oda says has answered every boat that ever came home here, is lashed shut. Go up and ask who lashed it.

Wenna Garrow, the lane-warden, won't unlash the horn while the Wrack Light is dark: a horn answered is a lane promised, and the Teeth are out there in the fog. The Wrack Light stands on its stack out on the Teeth. At the bottom of a spring tide, she says, the Teeth come up enough to walk, if you know where to put your feet. She knew, once. The tide isn't down.

Nobody ever knew the way across the Teeth by heart, Wenna says: every spring the lampwardens painted a mark of white lead on each rock that would bear you, a hand wide, and you put your feet on the white. The fog will have had the marks off, the way it had the Gannet's board. Tonight is the bottom of the springs. Go out to the end of the spit and wait the tide down.

Across the Teeth on the white, up the Wrack's stair. Its lantern room is framed in the timbers of boats that never came home, each with the yard's lead tag still nailed on: a year and a tide, and then the Wrack. One bracket is new and empty. The cradle is cold, and leaned to your ember and gave up: it wants something somebody on Wrackholm holds. Whatever feeds it, Wrackholm will never remember again. Wenna has her answer; the yard has the Gannet's board; Jory, maybe, has something of his brother's.
